messages:
tess: Heads-up while testing the new RN sample: hitting weird module-resolution + auth retry issues when using the JS SDK in Expo managed. ESM vs CJS looks implicated.

hugo: can you paste the exact error? metro/packager logs?

tess: main error during hot reload: `TypeError: Cannot read property 'headers' of undefined` coming from our retry interceptor. On cold start it works. Stack points to `node-fetch` shim calling `response.clone()` maybe being polyfilled incorrectly.

maya: suspicious. If Metro pulls the CJS build that polyfills fetch differently, our SDK's retry layer might be wrapping a different fetch instance than the app-level auth header injector. That yields undefined headers on cloned responses.

sam: RN + Expo use a global fetch. If the SDK bundles its own minimal fetch wrapper in the CJS bundle it can create two different fetch worlds. ESM builds are more likely to let bundlers dedupe. Do you have conditional exports in package.json?

tess: package.json currently only has "main" -> dist/index.cjs.js and "module" -> dist/index.mjs. No "react-native" export.

hugo: add a react-native export pointing to a tiny RN entry that re-exports the SDK but imports the app-level fetch polyfills and auth middleware first. That ensures single fetch identity and consistent headers used by retry.

maya: also watch for `whatwg-fetch` vs `cross-fetch` vs Expo's global. For auth/retry we rely on response.clone() semantics. Some polyfills implement clone shallowly and drop custom properties. Force the RN entry to use `global.fetch = fetch` from the same source you expect.

tess: good call. There's also TS weirdness: RN sample TS complains about `import Redwood from '@redwood/inference'` unless esModuleInterop true. Users on strict TS don't want to enable that. How should we publish?

sam: publish ESM-first with `export default` types and a named-cjs `export =` compatibility. In package.json use conditional exports: "exports": {".": {"import":"./dist/index.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs.js","react-native":"./dist/rn/index.js"}} and ship `dist/index.d.ts` with `export default` and named exports. That lets modern TS consumers avoid esModuleInterop.

hugo: one more: ensure the RN entry doesn't lazy-import the auth middleware. It should synchronously attach the fetch interceptor so hot reload doesn't create a temporal hole where the SDK makes a request without auth and the retry layer then fails.

tess: repro steps I added to the sample README: 1) expo init -> install sdk (linked workspace) 2) run `expo start` -> open in simulator -> trigger quick code change -> observe retry crash. I pushed a draft PR with `dist/rn/index.js` that imports `./setup-fetch` first.

maya: nice. dev tip: in setup-fetch do `const fetchImpl = require('cross-fetch'); global.fetch = fetchImpl; require('whatwg-fetch');` and attach an auth wrapper that sets Authorization on outbound requests. Keep it tiny and synchronous.

sam: also add a short note in onboarding docs about TS `compilerOptions.moduleResolution` and the importance of picking the right Expo SDK / Metro version that respects conditional exports.

dev-bot: CI note: sample-app-e2e flagged flaky http-auth tests on expo-managed iOS. Ticket #912 created.

tess: thanks all. I'll land the RN export + sync fetch setup and update the sample docs. Will follow up if flakes persist. :rocket:
